references.text: The context of this verse: It was the Jews in Jerusalem who sent priests and Levites to John to ask him who he was ([ref:Joh 1:19|John 1:19]).
The Pharisees consistently showed a hostile and investigative attitude toward religious movements they did not control, as they also did toward Jesus ([ref:Joh 7:47-49|John 7:47-49]).
The Pharisees acted as religious investigators and judges, just as they examined the healing of the man born blind ([ref:Joh 9:13-16|John 9:13-16]).

Gamaliel, a Pharisee and teacher of the law, stood up in the Council and spoke – this shows the influence of the Pharisees in Jewish governing bodies, which is also reflected in their sending people to interrogate John ([ref:Apg 5:34|Acts 5:34]).
According to Matthew as well, the Pharisees came to John at the Jordan, confirming that they were actively engaged in investigating his ministry ([ref:Matt 3:7|Matthew 3:7]).
The Pharisees and religious leaders questioned John's baptism and his authority, which parallels the interrogation in this verse ([ref:Matt 21:25|Matthew 21:25]).
The Pharisees rejected John's baptism and did not let themselves be baptized by him, providing background for their critical attitude when they sent envoys to examine him ([ref:Luk 7:30|Luke 7:30]).
